rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Setup 3 Game play (6 card variant) 4 Scoring 5 Variants 5.1 Card Power Objective The objective is for players to have the lowest value of the cards in front of them by either swapping them for lesser value cards or by pairing them up with cards of equal rank. Setup Option Values Description Number of grid cards 4 Arrange 4 dealt cards in a square and peek 2 cards. Use 1 deck. Closing ends a round. When players replace a card on their board with a newly drawn card, they are placed face down. 6 Arrange 6 dealt cards in 2x3 grid and flip 2 cards. Use 1 deck in 2/3/4/5-player and 2 decks in 6/7/8-player. Completing a full face up grid ends a round. 9 Arrange 9 dealt cards in a square and flip 3 cards. Use 1 deck in 2/3-player, 2 decks in 4/5/6-player and 3 decks in 7/8-player. Completing a full face up grid ends a round. Card power On If a card with power is drawn from the deck, it can either be used as a normal card or be discarded to use its power. J ⇨ peek at one of your face down cards. Q ⇨ peek at one of your opponent's face down cards. K ⇨ swap any two cards. Off Default selection Six cards are dealt face down to each player in two rows and three columns: 🟔 🟔 🟔 🟔 🟔 🟔 Game play (6 card variant) Each player flips two of their cards face up. The player on the dealer's left starts. Players take turns drawing a single card from either the face down deck or the top card of the face up discard pile. If the card is swapped for one of the face down cards, the card swapped in remains face up . The round ends when a player (the "closer") has all their cards face up. Every other player has one more turn, after which all cards are turned face up. Scoring Card A 2 3 ~ 10 J , Q K Points 1 -2 3 ~ 10 10 0 Add up all the values of face up cards. Any column or row of the same rank cancels out to zero. A 2x2 square of equal cards scores -20 points, ignoring normal card scores (even if the equal cards are bonus point cards). Example K♠ 6♠ K♥ 4♦ 6♥ 2♣ The column of 6♠ 6♥ cancel out to zero. Kings are worth zero. This scores +4 ( 4♦ ) -2 ( 2♣ ) = 2 points . The player with the fewest points wins the round. The player with the fewest cumulative points from all rounds wins the game. Variants Card Power When you draw a J, Q or K from the deck and immediately discard it, you can activate the corresponding power: J: Peek at 1 of your cards. Q: Peek at 1 of an opponent's card. K: Swap any 2 cards.

---

Golf is a card game played with one or more standard 52-card decks plus jokers, depending on the number of players. Generally, the game is played over 9 or 18 rounds, and the goal is to get the lowest score over those rounds.

Each player is dealt cards in a 2x3 or 2x4 rectangle. On a turn, a player will replace one card out of the draw or discard pile to try to lower their score. A matched pair (top to bottom) is worth 0 points, pip cards are worth their number, face cards are worth 10, but kings are worth 0. When one player decides to stop, the other players get one more chance to lower their score before the round ends.

There are restrictions on which cards can be played depending on which version of Golf you are playing. Many versions of Golf have evolved over the years, as happens with many standard card games.
community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] On the one hand, it can be played with a deck of cards -- but on the other hand, it can take over an hour with more players, and just isn't worth the time investment.

[Rating: 1/10] Was at one of my gaming groups. We were figuring out what to play next until someone awkwardly asked "So do you guys like to play... cards?", to which we very confusedly replied "Yes...?", because cards are a common feature of games, so it seemed obvious. He then pulled out a poker deck and suggested Golf. None of us have ever heard of Golf, so we decided to give it a shot, but little did I know: You don't play Golf. Golf plays you.

[Rating: 1/10] This is a high luck game albeit with some memory elements. There are many better card games out there.

[Rating: 2/10] Irritating memory game that, when no mistakes are made, relies on lucky drafts.  Winner is the player that has the opportunity to draw/draft the most appropriate cards without screwing up.  Perhaps this can be said about many games, but few are as transparent as this.

[Rating: 2/10] What did I do to be so cursed that the only "games" my extended family likes to play are horrible travesties such as this? Really, I'd rather just sit around and talk about the weather. The real tragedy is that they've taught it to my kids. (Fortunately, my kids love to play games where you actually do something.)

[Rating: 2/10] Lack of strategy or interaction, frustrating to "lose" but not satisfying to "win". Just throw a standard deck of cards on the table and shuffle them around if you need something mindless to do so you don't have to really pay attention to your family.

[Rating: 2.2/10] card management game with an aim to achieve lowest score too random and meaningless decision with lots of idle time

[Rating: 3/10] This is a classic game that I played solitaire, but there are so many better solitaire games.  Why would I play this one?

[Rating: 3/10] Played a multi-player version (four cards dealt to each player 2 which are face down).  Somewhat enjoyable but not enough decision making & too much luck for my taste.

[Rating: 3/10] This is just not my cup of tea.  There is too much luck in the hidden cards, and it's just kind of silly overall.

[Rating: 3/10] Please, PLEASE don't force me to play this game again, oh sigh, here we go again... But at least it's better than Mexican Train, and if those are the only two choices...

[Rating: 3/10] After 5+ Plays: I remember this game slightly differently than the description here, as we played with a 3x3 grid.  But regardless of the shape, this is a boring game.

[Rating: 3/10] We played a variation (actually the base rules at pagat.com) in which you can't look at all your cards, which made it more interesting.

[Rating: 3/10] A fun game for the extended family that allows for a lot of people. However, there is not quite enough decisions for me to like it.

[Rating: 3/10] Parents and their friends like this game so I play it with them - and that's the only reason I'd play it.

[Rating: 3/10] Played a 2x2 variant of this card game.  Like a lot of card games, it's very luck dependent, though counting cards does have some benefits.
